items.title: Energy Storage Systems Guide
items.summary:
At a basic level an energy storage system stores electricity produced by a generation source such as a solar array or the grid and then dispatches that power when needed. Key components typically include batteries a power conversion system such as an inverter control electronics and a management system that communicates with inverters and a home energy management device. [...] Resilience and backup power Energy storage systems provide a source of electricity during utility outages supporting essential loads and improving day to day reliability.
 Cost management Stored energy can be used during peak price periods or time of use rate spikes to reduce utility bills depending on local rate structures.
 Increased self consumption By using energy produced on site more of the solar output is consumed rather than exported to the grid which can improve overall economics. [...] # Energy Storage Systems for Home and Business

Nov 9, 2026

Energy storage systems are becoming a central part of modern home and commercial energy strategies. Paired with rooftop solar and smart electrical upgrades these systems store excess generation for use during peak hours outages or times when the sun is not producing. This article explains how energy storage systems work which benefits to expect and what to consider when evaluating options.

items.title: Solar Integration: Solar Energy and Storage Basics | Department of Energy
items.summary: “Storage” refers to technologies that can capture electricity, store it as another form of energy (chemical, thermal, mechanical), and then release it for use when it is needed. Lithium-ion batteries are one such technology. Although using energy storage is never 100% efficient—some energy is always lost in converting energy and retrieving it—storage allows the flexible use of energy at different times from when it was generated. So, storage can increase system efficiency and resilience, and it [...] The most common type of energy storage in the power grid is pumped hydropower. But the storage technologies most frequently coupled with solar power plants are electrochemical storage (batteries) with PV plants and thermal storage (fluids) with CSP plants. Other types of storage, such as compressed air storage and flywheels, may have different characteristics, such as very fast discharge or very large capacity, that make them attractive to grid operators. items.title: ICLEI South Asia, in collaboration with @UNDRR, @UNDP and @cdri_world, organised a three-day training and peer exchange
items.summary:
ICLEI South Asia, in collaboration with @UNDRR, @UNDP and @cdri_world, organised a three-day training and peer exchange workshop on Inclusive Climate Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) in Cities on 2-4 November 2026, in Bangkok, Thailand. 

City officials from 10 municipalities across Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Sri Lanka attended technical sessions and exchanged local experiences and best practices to strengthen regional cooperation on resilience and #DRR. 

The training sessions focused on climate resilience planning and DRR, integrating Gender and Social Inclusivity (#GESI) into local planning frameworks, ecosystem-based adaptation (EbA), nature-based solutions (#NbS) in resilience planning, locally-led adaptation (LLA) in risk reduction, resilient infrastructure planning, development and governance, financing climate and disaster resilience, practical applications of the DRR Scorecard developed by UNDRR, and a panel discussion on Inclusive Climate Resilience Practices, focusing on extreme heat and health.

Participants also visited the Bang Sue Education and Environmental Conservation Center, operated by the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA), to learn about their municipal wastewater management system through the integration of grey, green and blue infrastructure in Bangkok. 

🔷The training marked the completion of a year-long #capacitybuilding programme for city officials under the ‘Climate and Development Knowledge Network (@cdknetwork) – Accelerating Inclusive Action,’ supported and funded by the 𝗠𝗶𝗻𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆 𝗼𝗳 𝗙𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗔𝗳𝗳𝗮𝗶𝗿𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗡𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀 and @IDRC_CRDI through the #StepChange Initiative. The initiative has equipped city officials with practical knowledge and institutional capacity for assessing, planning, financing, implementing, and monitoring local climate and DRR actions.

#ClimateAction #DisasterRiskReduction
